review_title: It’s very good. Integrations make it indispensable.
review_text:
Todoist is an excellent task manager on its own. It’s clean, intuitive, reliable, and does a great job of keeping everything organized without getting in the way.

But where it really shines is its integrations, particularly with AI like Grok and ChatGPT. These integrations transform Todoist from a simple to-do list into a powerful productivity hub.

For example, I recently dictated a messy 16-item checklist for preparing a house to sell. Through ChatGPT, I turned that stream of thoughts into a structured Todoist project, complete with individually actionable tasks, sections, and due dates. 

WHILE DRIVING. 

No tedious manual entry, copying and pasting, or jumping between apps. I can also ask Grok or ChatGPT to add individual tasks with deadlines directly to my Todoist Inbox.

Did I mention you can do all of this with the free version? 

Todoist’s new feature (ramble?) does do great figuring out what you mean in dictation, and reasoning - but being able to have a meandering voice conversation with Grok or ChatGPT and having it turn into a concrete project on Todoist is just absolute next level stuff. 

Todoist is great on its own, but its extensibility and seamless integration into my broader workflow are what make it indispensable. Five stars.

Structured absolutely needs a search function. The premium version needs a way to prevent tons of duplicates from stacking on top of each other. Some pop-up asking if you meant to create a duplicate if the task already exists on a day would be nice. The AI in the premium version isn't very helpful. 

Structured has a checklist with a nice widget and some fun icons to make seeing the tasks easier at a glance.

It has some disadvantages that other apps, such as FlowSavvy, don't have. Some of those disadvantages are: Structured has no search function at all (not even in the premium version), overlapping tasks creating a visual mess (FlowSavvy stacks them next to each other if they overlap, instead of directly above/below as Structured does), and no repeating tasks unless you have premium (FlowSavvy lets you repeat tasks on the free version). 

The search function for Structured has been on their roadmap for almost 4 years. The allowance for overlapping tasks that don't disturb the task flow has been on the roadmap for almost 3 years and was rejected, with no clear reason given.

That said, Structured is quite reasonably priced and even has a lifetime purchase option.

This app has been ruined, not to mention the ridiculous price increase for what should be normal features.

review_title: I LOVE This App, but the Inbox Is HORRIBLY PAINFUL! Please end the suffering!
review_text:
I absolutely love this app except for one thing: The Inbox.

If it wasn’t for the inbox, I would give this app five stars. In fact, I would give it more if I could.

The Inbox is so painful to use on a tablet and especially on a phone if you have a lot of items sitting there that you haven’t scheduled yet. And isn’t that the whole point of an inbox? I put things there because I know I need to do them, I don’t want to forget them, but I don’t necessarily know yet when I’m going to do them.

I currently have around 20 things in my Inbox, and trying to organize them is incredibly frustrating. You have to press and hold each task and drag it where you want it. But if you’re trying to move something farther up the list, once you reach the top of the screen, IT DOESN’T KEEP SCROLLING. It just stops. So you have to let go of the task, scroll the list to make more room at the top, find the task again, drag it farther up, and keep repeating this process.

Why???

There’s also no way to filter or sort the Inbox by category, which would at least make managing a larger Inbox easier.

What frustrates me so much is that I genuinely LOVE this app. I have a lot of plates spinning in my life, with both big and little things I need to remember, and Structured is exactly the kind of app I need. But I’m starting to wonder if the Inbox is actually helping me manage all of those things or just giving me another frustrating list that I have to manage.

Please fix this user experience. At the very least, tasks should continuously scroll when you drag them to the top or bottom of the screen. Even better, give us ways to sort, filter, group, or otherwise organize the Inbox.

I design software, so I understand that development takes time and priorities have to be made. But this feels like such a fundamental usability issue in a core part of the app. Please make it a priority.

I really don’t want to stop using Structured because I love almost everything else about it. But the Inbox is making me want to.

I’ve been using Evernote for 7 years (since 2019) as a paid professional service, and I have seen severe performance degradation over the last 2-3 years. I got a notice that they increased my yearly subscription price from $140 to $240 - on the same day I couldn’t get a note to open on my phone because of an aforementioned new performance issue. I didn’t mind the price increase alone, but Evernote’s service is now full of AI slop and unacceptable software development practices.

For a replacement, I considered Joplin, Notesnook, and Obsidian. 
Notesnook is user friendly, boasts the same core features as Evernote without the slop, adds additional nice-to-have features like nesting notebooks, and the syncing is flawless between my devices.

I would highly recommend you skip this buggy app that won’t be able to load a simple text note because it’s trying to AI-generate something you didn’t ask for. Instead, save a couple hundred dollars and go with a more reliable, functional, and quality service.

review_text:
I’m a college student. I’ve been using OneNote since high school to take notes. I’ve had the same iPad since then. It worked for the most part—but I’ve had to deal with obnoxious bugs throughout my years using the app. (auto-deselecting a marker when I use my Apple Pencil to write, extremely clunky syncing making it difficult to access my notes, version differences appearing for no reason, etc.) They’ve never made the app literally unusable until now. 

In the past month, I discovered that the app wasn’t syncing with my laptop version of OneNote. I tried to sign in with my University Microsoft account, and it didn’t work. I just got stuck. I tried uninstalling but that didn’t fix it- instead it just locked me out of taking notes on my iPad at all. I tried installing PowerPoint as a workaround but I had to install an older version due to my iPad’s age and it has this problem too. I looked into it online and other people have been having this problem, but most people say it’s been fixed with the newest update. 

Here’s the problem: you pushed the recent update that caused the issue, but then you limited the update that actually *fixes* the issue to IOS 18 and above. Three months ago I could take notes just fine. Now my iPad is apparently obsolete. I don’t know if you can push updates that are compatible with older versions, but if you can, please fix this. I literally cannot use the app without it and this planned obsolescence outcome is absolutely infuriating.

review_title: Poor implementation of access to photos
review_text:
iOS gives developers better options than what OneNote appears to be using here. An app can present Apple’s private photo picker, where you can choose any photo at that moment without granting the app permanent access to your whole library. Many apps do exactly that.

With Limited Access, an app can also provide a “Select More Photos” / “Manage Photos” button that invokes iOS’s permission screen from inside the app. OneNote apparently isn’t giving you that convenient path—or isn’t handling the modern picker correctly.

So the awkward workflow you’re seeing is not an unavoidable iPhone limitation. It’s largely a OneNote behavior/design issue.

One workaround worth trying is:

Photos → select photo → Share → OneNote

That hands the specific photo to OneNote directly and normally shouldn’t require OneNote to have general access to the photo library.

Otherwise, Full Access is unfortunately the least irritating solution if you frequently insert photos into OneNote.

review_title: Best app to keep track of things
review_text:
I've used many different apps including Evernote and others. This is the best app and here's why. The app is available for your mobile phone, your windows computer (possibly for Mac also), and on the Internet if you are using someone else's computer. The note taking ability is made easy by the fact that you can have multiple notebooks. Within each notebook you can have multiple tabs (for a topic or area of interest), and within the tabs you can have multiple pages, each page can be its own little nugget of information. It beats having to save emails and word docs on your computer, then opening each one for the exact info you are looking for. OneNote has its search bar that will search all notebooks for you. And best thing is it auto-saves! Just type your info and close the app! On your mobile phone, hit the sync button if you want to see it instantaneously update your desktop app. The latest enhancement allows me to take a picture on my phone and save it directly to my Notes. No more guessing where I saw that article and/or wishing I had a copy to send to people. Amazing. Love it. Thank you, developers/designers at Microsoft. There is ONE thing I do want to see as a feature enhancement - allow the MOBILE app to allow searching within the page. Currently only the desktop version has the ability to search within the page or within the entire application. UPDATE - there is a SECOND feature that is missing that’s really useful- the ability to add a row to a table, on the mobile app. Easily done on the desktop app but impossible on the mobile app - the moment you hit enter, it creates a new line within the cell of the table and not a new row. 
FIX these two deficiencies and it’ll be a 5-star app.

I used Evernote for 10–12 years and spent about eight of those meaning to find a better alternative.
Disclaimer: I always used the free plan, so yes, I’m complaining about a free service. But Evernote’s longstanding two-device limit never made upgrading feel like a value-add. It felt like ransom for the privilege of accessing my own notes across devices like it isn’t 2012.
I didn’t use it heavily: maybe 150 notes across 10 notebooks—recipes, clothing sizes, part numbers, quotations, and other small things I wanted to keep. I mostly treated it as a notebook that lived on my phone.
Today I opened Evernote to find a recipe and discovered the free tier had become dramatically more restrictive—roughly one notebook and 50 notes. I couldn’t even properly access my existing collection without accepting a seven-day trial that would begin billing about $250 per year.
So I spent the morning screenshotting notes, copying and pasting them elsewhere, and occasionally exporting them in Evernote’s proprietary format. Then I canceled the trial and deleted the app.
I will happily pay for Notion or Obsidian Sync. I will not give money to a company that uses access to my existing notes as leverage.

Congratulations, Evernote: you freed up about 5 MB of storage today. A small part of me hopes that same 5 MB eventually stores your Chapter 11 filing.

review_title: Runs HOT & Drains battery like crazy
review_text:
So I really did use to love this app, so much so that I’ve been using the premium version for over a year now actually, however it’s no longer worth it unfortunately… 

Within the past few months anytime I open the app on my phone now it starts to drain my battery like crazy. I’m talking every 30 seconds I loose one percent battery at least! And that’s just if I have the app open. Once I start trying to actually time block too then my phone starts to get super glitchy & run extremely hot as well. So hot that only after a few min of using the app my phone will soon be burning my hands up & I’ll have to let it cool off before I can use it again. This is not normal! 

At first I thought maybe my phones battery was just starting to go bad since I’ll admit I may not have the newest iPhone on the market, & sure my battery isn’t as great as it once was, but this is in fact the only app that causes me problems & force closing this application is the only thing that instantly solves all those problems. Therefore it’s definitely not exclusively an issue with my battery, but rather within the app itself. 

Ultimately I’m not sure what bug randomly brought this on, but I suspect that if I do attempt to keep using this app then I really will start to have issues with my phones battery as no app should ever cause a phone to get that hot!
Especially a simple calendar app you’d think?

That said, sadly I’m left with no other choice than to cancel my yearly membership & delete this glitchy thing off my phone ASAP before it has the chance to do anymore damage. The only reason I haven’t deleted it yet is cuz I was hoping the next update would resolve these issues. Alas, multiple app updates later, including multiple phone updates later, & I’m still having problems so I simply can’t risk it anymore. Clearly this bug isn’t going away…

review_title: Watch out! They’ll hold your data hostage!
review_text:
I was a loyal Evernote user for years. I paid for premium, built my entire note system in it, and trusted the platform with a significant amount of personal and professional data.

I eventually moved to Microsoft OneNote because it’s more affordable and, frankly, has surpassed Evernote in both usability and value.

Coming back now to retrieve my data has been a frustrating and disappointing experience. Features that used to be standard are now locked behind aggressive limitations. The web app refuses access due to notebook limits. Device restrictions prevent normal syncing. The overall experience feels intentionally designed to make it difficult to leave without paying again.

Call it what you want, but from a user perspective it feels like my own data is being held behind artificial barriers.

I understand companies need to monetize, but there’s a difference between charging for features and creating friction around data access. This approach erodes trust and punishes long-time users who simply want to move on.

I would strongly recommend that anyone considering Evernote think carefully about long-term data ownership and exit costs. Getting your information in is easy. Getting it out is another story.

review_title: pros might not outweigh the cons
review_text:
TLDR Summary: it probably isn't worth the hefty price tag. 

Cons:
-The price has doubled twice in three years. $21/month is what you'll have to pay to sync your notes on your phone, iPad, laptop and work desktop. If you can get by with three devices, you might be able to squeak by on the Starter plan.
- One of the new "updates" by promoted by the developer is a new pricing plan. What a spin! You're telling me that one of the new "features" I have to pay for is a more expensive pricing structure?
-Another new feature is the AI inclusion, meaning that machine learning will be used to read and sort your information. Only on the Enterprise plan is ownership of data guaranteed; check the privacy policy for how they determine ownership of what you upload. What you upload will be shared with OpenAi and other unnamed third parties, meaning that those audio files will share what your voice sounds like with an undisclosed third party. 
-In the phone app, you can export or download a note as a psf file. The only way to share is via a link or email.

Pros:
-The Web Clipper browser extension. I've found it incredibly useful to be able to save pages and paragraphs from websites.
-Scannable. The ability to convert image-to-text or image-to-pdf has been helpful, although it's a bummer the Scannable app costs extra.
-Handwritting recognition? I don't use handwriting features often, but I like the idea of converting ink to digital format (replacing all of the Rocketbooks and smart notebooks I've tried with a regular old pen & paper). 

Neutral: Some features are a given with any note-taking app and I'm listing them here so it's clear why they don't help a consumer choose Evernote:
-Tags to sort your content 
-Notebooks to organize by subject (Only 20 if you're using the Starter plan)
-Templates
-Calendar integration (but tbh this is done better by the apps with strong email integration like Microsoft OneNote or Google imho)

Then, a badly implemented update caused a piece of writing I had worked on for hours to, with an easy keyboard stumble, be completely rewritten. Completely. Hours of work chewed up and spit out into slush. :/ I promptly closed the app and stopped writing in it.  

Years later, I have found a software I like better, with no intrusive ai and no cloud services, so my notes are no longer at risk in a server I don't have access to. I have zero faith that notion has kept anything I ever wrote secure. They continue to say one thing and do another. I am done. 

In logging in to transfer my notes, I notice that the program is buggy and slow in ways it never was years ago. Buffers like crazy. It's actually kind of heartbreaking to see how far this app has fallen.

There are better options out there, with more security and better customization. Even if you want ai in a notes app, there are more clean and helpful options that do not compromise your experience. Why pick notion? I never will again.

Please resolve these simple UX flaws to further improve the app. It’s pretty good but feels rough around the edges as is. I am using the latest version for Apple OS on an iPhone.
